# DESIGN.md — Business 0d3158d5-cdb4-4908-b0bf-9aab2692362b

archetype: garden-daylight
rationale: This café has no photographs, menu, hours or story yet, so its deep-green-and-cream branding has to carry the whole site. Garden-daylight lets those two colours read as a calm daytime café through an open cream ground, a sage arch around the logo and unhurried type, and it produces an honest one-screen-and-a-form site that invents nothing to fill the gaps.
interaction_level: L1

personality: [unhurried, fresh, casual, quietly modern]

typography:
  display: "Larsseit"
  body: "Figtree"
  scale: 1.25
  notes: Larsseit carries the business name, the "Café" eyebrow and the contact heading. It is set in medium weight rather than bold so it stays soft. Line-height is 1.15 on display and 1.65 on body for airy leading. Eyebrows are small caps at 0.8rem with 0.12em tracking. Body text is never below 1.0625rem. The business name is long, so it is set at a moderate display size and never shouted. It is rendered exactly as given, character for character. It wraps at its hyphens, which browsers break after naturally. Add overflow-wrap: anywhere only as a fallback so it can never overflow the column.

palette:
  primary: "#273728"
  secondary: "#041F2C"
  accent: "#F8F3E7"
  ground: "#FCFAF4"
  surface: "#EEF0E6"
  ink: "#18231A"
  muted: "#4E5D50"
  border: "#D9DDD0"
  application: The page ground is a pale daylight cream (#FCFAF4), so the site reads as morning, not evening.
    - Primary (#273728) carries the h1, the hero button and the contact band behind the form.
    - Accent (#F8F3E7) is the button text and the contact-band text on primary, at about 11:1. It is never used on the light ground, where it would vanish.
    - Secondary (#041F2C) is reserved for the footer strip and for focus rings on the cream ground.
    - Inside the primary contact band, focus rings switch to accent with a 2px offset so they stay visible against the green.
    - Surface (#EEF0E6) is a sage step from the ground, used for the hero arch.
    - Ink is the brand green pushed down to near-black.
    - Muted (#4E5D50) passes about 6.7:1 on the ground and 6:1 on the surface.
    - These neutrals form a cream-and-sage pair drawn straight from the brand's own green and cream, not a stock grey ramp.

composition:
  whitespace: generous
  photography: none
  card_usage: none
  mobile: The hero arch narrows to 80vw and sits above the text instead of beside it. The name drops to 1.75rem and wraps at its hyphens. The button goes full width. The contact form's two-column field row collapses to a single column. There is no sticky bar.

composition: There is nothing to sell yet beyond the café's identity and a way to reach it. So the page leads with the mark and the brand's own daylight colour, makes no claims, and points every move at the one honest next step: getting in touch. There is no menu, no hours and no story to fake. Their absence is the design's restraint, not a gap to pad.

sections:
  - id: hero
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: Within three seconds, say this is a café called Business 0d3158d5-cdb4-4908-b0bf-9aab2692362b, give the brand its daylight presence, and offer one step: getting in touch.
    spec: A two-column split on desktop, about 55/45, on the #FCFAF4 ground, filling roughly 85vh.
      - Right column: a tall arch, a rectangle with a fully rounded top like a garden doorway, filled with surface #EEF0E6.
        - The logo PNG, used verbatim, sits centred in the arch's upper half at about 220px wide.
        - A soft 1px #D9DDD0 inner outline runs 16px inside the arch edge.
        - This arch is the page's one distinctive moment.
      - Left column, bottom-aligned with the arch base, from top to bottom:
        - a small-caps eyebrow, "Café", in muted;
        - the h1, the business name exactly as given, in Larsseit medium at clamp(1.75rem, 3.6vw, 3rem), in primary;
        - one primary-filled button reading "Get in touch", with accent text and a 2px radius, linking to #contact.
      - No standfirst, tagline, hours, address or invented description.
      - The header holds only the logo at small size on the left and a "Contact" text link on the right.

  - id: contact
    priority: essential
    show: all
    intent: There is no phone, email or address to publish, so give anyone who wants to reach the café, with a question or an introduction, a real working route.
    spec: A full-width band in primary #273728 with accent #F8F3E7 type, anchored as #contact, with 8rem padding top and bottom on desktop.
      - Left third:
        - a Larsseit heading, "Say hello", at 2.25rem;
        - one plain line: "Send us a message and we'll get back to you."
        - No contact details are listed, because none exist.
      - Right two-thirds, the form:
        - Name and Email fields sit side by side, with a full-width Message textarea below.
        - Labels sit above the fields, in small caps, in accent.
        - Inputs have an explicit #F8F3E7 background, #18231A text, #4E5D50 placeholders and a 1px #D9DDD0 border.
        - Focus shows a 2px accent ring with a 2px offset, so it reads against the green band.
        - Below the fields come the reCAPTCHA v2 widget, then a submit button with accent fill and primary text.
        - A status line under the button, in accent, shows the success or failure message.
      - Behaviour:
        - The form posts JSON to {apiBaseUrl}/api/v1/public/forms/submit with form_type "contact".
        - Build form_data field by field (name, email, message), with captcha_token at the top level.
        - Load recaptcha/api.js lazily on the first focusin.
        - Validate name, email and message client-side before calling fetch.
      - On mobile the band becomes one column, with the heading above the stacked fields, and padding drops to 4rem.

avoid:
  - any mention of brunch, breakfast, coffee origins, dishes, prices or "open daily": none of it is in the content
  - a "Menu", "Visit us" or "Hours" nav item or section, since there is nothing behind them
  - stock avocado toast, latte art, or any image other than the supplied logo
  - leaf, sprig or botanical clip-art standing in for the missing photography; the sage arch is the only garden gesture
  - turning the whole page dark green; primary is a band and a structural colour, and the ground stays daylight cream
  - a centred hero over three cards, or a "Fresh · Local · Cozy" icon row
  - #F8F3E7 text or an accent-filled button on the cream ground, where it disappears
  - a secondary-colour focus ring inside the green contact band, where it cannot be seen
  - a newsletter signup or any form that shows success without the real fetch
